else because he needed his rest after some procedure or other had left him weak and in
pain. If I wanted Mom and Dad to watch me play soccer, I knew that nine out of ten times
they'd miss it because they were busy shuttling August to speech therapy or physical
therapy or a new specialist or a surgery.
Mom and Dad would always say I was the most understanding little girl in the world. I
don't know about that, just that I understood there was no point in complaining. I've seen
August after his surgeries: his little face bandaged up and swollen, his tiny body full of
tubes to keep him alive. After you've seen someone else going through that, it feels kind of
crazy to complain over not getting the toy you had asked for, or your mom missing a school
play. I knew this even when I was six years old. No one ever told it to me. I just knew it.
So I've gotten used to not complaining, and I've gotten used to not bothering Mom and
Dad with little stuff. I've gotten used to figuring things out on my own: how to put toys
together, how to organize my life so I don't miss friends' birthday parties, how to stay on
top of my schoolwork so I never fall behind in class. I've never asked for help with my
homework. Never needed reminding to finish a project or study for a test. If I was having
trouble with a subject in school, I'd go home and study it until I figured it out on my own. I
taught myself how to convert fractions into decimal points by going online. I've done every
school project pretty much by myself. When Mom or Dad ask me how things are going in
school, I've always said "good"—even when it hasn't always been so good. My worst day,
worst fall, worst headache, worst bruise, worst cramp, worst mean thing anyone could say
has always been nothing compared to what August has gone through. This isn't me being
noble, by the way: it's just the way I know it is.

다음 글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 대한 답을 영어로 쓰시오. [20점]
Life is a mysterious journey, full of unexpected twists and turns that shape our destiny. At
times, we may think we have a clear direction, but then fate intervenes and leads us on an
entirely different path. Such is the case for David Swan. David Swan was on his way to
Boston to work at his uncle's store. After traveling on foot from sunrise until nearly noon on
a hot summer day, he grew tired. He searched for a shady spot to rest and await the coming
of the stagecoach. He soon found a small cluster of maples that provided a nice place to rest
and nap, with a fresh, bubbling spring. He used his small bag of clothes as a pillow and soon
fell asleep.
After a short while, a carriage stopped in front of him as one of the wheels had slid off. As
the coachman and servant fixed the wheel, an old couple sheltered under the maple trees
and noticed the bubbling fountain with David asleep beside it. The old lady whispered to her
husband, "It seems like fate brought him here for a reason after our disappointment with our
cousin's son. I can even see a resemblance to our departed Henry. Should we wake him
up?" "Why?" her husband asked, "We know nothing of his character. What's your intention?"
"Since the death of our only offspring, we have none to leave our wealth when our time
comes," she responded. "Do you think he is as nice as he appears?" the husband asked.
"Yes, I think we should wake him up," his wife replied. As they were about to wake him up,
the servant called out, "The wheel is fixed. The carriage is ready to leave." The old couple felt
embarrassed for contemplating waking up the stranger and quickly departed.
As David continued to sleep, a pretty young girl stopped to adjust her skirt and noticed him
sleeping by the spring. A bee landed on David's eyelid, and the girl quickly removed it with
her handkerchief. Her face turned red as she took a glance at him and thought "He is
handsome!" Little did she know her wealthy father was looking for a young man like David to
work for him and marry his daughter. If David had spoken to the girl, he could have become
her father's clerk and, eventually, married her. Once again, David was unaware of the
opportunity for love that was so dose to him.
Shortly after the girl was out of sight, two shady-looking men appeared. They were known
to steal from others and noticed David's bag under his head. One of them suggested, "Do
you see that bundle under his head? I'll bet you he has money in that bag. Let's take it." The

I(Opal) ate my Littmus Lozenge slow.  It tasted good.  It tasted like root beer and
strawberry and something else I didn’t have a name for, something that made me feel kind
of sad. I looked over at Amanda. She was sucking on her candy and thinking hard.
“Do you like it?” Miss Franny asked me.
“Yes ma’am,” I told her.
“What about you, Amanda? Do you like the Littmus Lozenge?”
“Yes ma’am,” she said. “But it makes me think of things I feel sad about.”
I wondered what in the world Amanda Wilkinson had to feel sad about. She wasn’t new
to town. She had a mama and a daddy. I had seen her with them in church.
“There’s a secret ingredient in there,” Miss Franny said.
“I know it,” I told her. “I can taste it. What is it?”
“Sorrow,” Miss Franny said. “Not everybody can taste it. Children, especially, seem to
have a hard time knowing it’s there.”
“I taste it,” I said.
“Me, too,” said Amanda.
“Well, then,” Miss Franny said, “you’ve probably both had your share of sadness.”
“I had to move away from Watley and leave all my friends,” I said. “That is one sadness
I have had. And Dunlap and Stevie Dewberry are always picking on me. That’s another
sadness. And the biggest one, my biggest sadness, is that my mama left me when I
was still small. And I can hardly remember her; I keep hoping I’ll get to meet her and tell
her some stories.”

TEXT A
(Doctor De Soto, a kind and skilled mouse dentist, risks treating a dangerous fox with a
toothache.)
The next morning, promptly at eleven, a very cheerful fox turned up. He was not feeling
a particle of pain. When Doctor De Soto got into his mouth, he snapped it shut for a moment,
then opened wide and laughed. “Just a joke!” he chortled. “Be serious,” said the dentist
sharply. “We have work to do.” His wife, also a mouse, was lugging the heavy tooth up the
ladder.
“Oh, I love it!” exclaimed the fox. “It’s just beautiful.” Doctor De Soto set the gold tooth in
its socket and hooked it up to the teeth on both sides. The fox caressed the new tooth with
his tongue.
“My, it feels good,” he thought. “I really shouldn’t eat them. On the other hand, how can
I resist?” “We’re not finished,” said Doctor De Soto, holding up a large jug.
“I have here a remarkable preparation developed only recently by my wife and me. With
just one application, you can be rid of toothaches forever. How would you like to be the first
one to receive this unique treatment?” “I certainly would!” the fox declared. “I’d be honored.”
He hated any kind of personal pain. “You will never have to see us again,” said Doctor De
Soto. “No one will ever see you again,” said the fox to himself.
He had definitely made up his mind to eat them—with the help of his brand-new tooth.
Doctor De Soto stepped into the fox’s mouth with a bucket of secret formula and proceed
to paint each tooth. He hummed as he worked. Mrs. De Soto stood by on the ladder, pointing
out spots he had missed. The fox looked very happy. When the dentist was done, he
stepped out. “Now close your jaws tight,” he said, “and keep them closed for a full minute.”
The fox did as he was told.
Then he tried to open his mouth—but his teeth were stuck together! “Ah excuse me, I
should have mentioned,” said Doctor De Soto, “you won’t be able to open your mouth for a
day or two. The secret formula must first permeate the dentine. But don’t worry. No pain
ever again!”
The fox was stunned. He stared at Doctor De Soto, then at his wife. They smiled and
waited. All he could do was say, “Fank oo berry mush” through his clenched teeth, and get
up and leave. He tried to do so with dignity. Then he stumbled down the stairs in a daze.

When darkness fell, the tiger showed up in front of the house. He envisioned a tasty
dinner of red bean porridge and the granny. While the poor woman was trembling with
fear, the tiger went straight to the kitchen to look for the red bean porridge. When he
stooped down to find a pot, the chestnut, covered with hot ash, sprang out of the stove
and hit the tiger in the eye. The tiger was so startled that he almost jumped out of his
skin. To wash his burning eye, the tiger put his head in a big water jar standing next to
the stove. As if waiting for this to happen, the turtle in the jar bit the tiger’s face hard.
Frightened, the tiger stormed out of the kitchen, only to slip on the dog poop in the
kitchen doorway. Just at that moment, a mortar pestle from above fell right on his head.
The tiger fell flat on his back, and the straw mat rolled him up tight. Then, the A-frame
carrier in the yard carried the tiger wrapped in the straw mat on its back and ran toward
the river. There, the straw mat unfurled before pushing the tiger in the water.

논술형
다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 조건을 참고하여, 재구성하시오.
Trysdale stood in his room. The green cactus on the table, with its inviting, swaying leaves,
reminded him of what he had lost. Also in the room was Trysdales’ best friend, who was also
the bride’s brother. He chatted nearby, unaware of Trysdale’s torment.
The wedding had been painful. The bride, once his love, had walked the aisle pale but
radiant. As she looked at her groom with shining eyes, Trysdale knew she had forgotten
him. His once-impenetrable pride now lay in ruins, replaced by bitter self-awareness. Why
had their romance ended this way? They hadn’t fought with each other even once.
For the thousandth time, he replayed the last days of their relationship in his mind. He
constantly tried to find the reason that everything had ended so suddenly.
He recalled their last happy moment: his proposal. Now it was too painful to think of her
beauty that night. It was her beauty that had always made him accept her praise. During
their conversation she said, “Captain Carruthers says that you speak Spanish like a native
speaker. Is there anything you aren’t good at?”
It occurred to Trysdale that he had repeated an old Spanish saying to Carruthers. He had
heard  it from somewhere by chance and then said  it  later, pretending to be smart.
Carruthers, who loved to exaggerate, must have overestimated Trysdale’s ability. However,
her praise was so sweet that he could not tell her the truth. He just let her continue
believing that he was a fluent speaker of Spanish.
How glad, how shy, how nervous she was when he proposed! How surprised she
seemed when he kneeled in front of her! The look in her eyes meant “yes.” However, she
avoided a direct response and shyly said, “I will send you my answer tomorrow.”
The next day, a cactus arrived instead of a reply, tagged with a strange name. He waited until
night, but her answer did not come. With his pride so deeply wounded, he did not try to visit
her. When they later met, their awkwardness turned cold, and their love faded.
Now, after her wedding, Trysdale still searched for answers. His friend’s voice broke the
silence. Spotting the cactus, the friend remarked, “Do you know Spanish, Trysdale? This tag
says ventomarme. The people there think the leaves of this cactus look like they are reaching
out and telling you to come. So, in English it means ‘Come and take me.’
출처: The Cactus, (O Henry, 1917)

예시 답안
Hello everyone.
Today,   I  will  discuss how  love  is  expressed  in "Romeo  and  Juliet"  and
"Chunhyangjeon." These works illustrate the distinct communication styles shaped
by their cultural contexts. First, in "Romeo and Juliet," Romeo's declaration to Juliet
is direct and clear. He says, "My bounty is as boundless as the sea, My love as
deep; the more  I give to thee, the more  I have, for both are infinite." This shows
the Western approach to openly expressing emotions.
Conversely,  in  "Chunhyangjeon,"  Mongryong  describes  his  affection  through
metaphors. He says, "Upon your face as lovely as a flower, the moon of my heart
has risen. Just as the moonlight shines upon the flowers, your face brightly glows."
This reflects the Eastern style of expressing feelings subtly and indirectly.
In sum, "Romeo and Juliet" and "Chunhyangjeon" both explore love but do so in
ways that mirror their cultural influences—directly in the West and indirectly in the
East. Thank you.

Dr. Sylvia Earle, a dedicated oceanographer, has spent over four decades at the frontier of
deep ocean exploration, during which time she has earned such laurels as Time’s first
“Hero for the Planet” and the designation of National Geographic Explorer-in-Residence.
Among the many ways in which she is propagating ideas about positive change for our
planet is through the work of her foundation, Mission Blue, whose objective is to protect
and restore the ocean through the creation of “Hope Spots”—designated areas of extreme
importance to the ocean’s overall well-being. In the following interview, Dr. Earle presents
some poignant observations to urge the public to take action regarding the plight of the
oceans.
(중략)
Q. In a situation that seems so severe, how are Hope Spots a cause for hope?
Dr. Earle: (a)The term Hope Spot was conceived to recognize that there are places in the
ocean and on the planet that have a huge significance in terms of their role in maintaining
the integrity of the systems we’ve talked about. We should do everything we can to
embrace pristine areas, places that are intact and that represent the distillation of  all
preceding history, where you have high diversity and a high level of functioning that hasn’t
been impacted. Hope Spots embrace these undefiled areas, but they extend beyond them
as well, to places that have been altered through human influence but that, if protected,
give us reasons to hope they can be restored, perhaps not to the way they were a thousand
years ago, but to a significantly better state than they are in now. This will only happen if we
take the pressure off and allow them to heal and recover. We have lost pieces, but the
wonderful thing about a healthy, natural system is its resilience. Even if a few pieces are
lost, they can regrow and recover so that the system is restored.

How Microbes Clean Up the Environment
Microbes are nature’s ultimate trash disposal, consuming and decomposing the dead
material that spreads over the earth’s surface. They do such a fabulous job that humans
have taken an increasing interest in getting them to clean up our environmental messes.
The concept involved in this process  is called bioremediation.  (b)It involves using
microbes that either naturally have a propensity to eat contaminants or have been
genetically altered to give them a taste for toxins. Scientists are designing and using
microbes to remove contaminants such as oil, radioactive waste, gasoline, and mercury,
and new bioremediation research appears regularly.

He, my father, had just given me a new penny, bright as gold. He took it from his
pocket several times, waiting for me to notice it.
“You can have it if you want it, Dan,” he said at last.
I said, “Oh, thanks.” Nothing more.
< 중략>
It was almost dark when their excited talking in the room woke me. It was mother who
had found me. “Danny!” she cried, “where have you been!” “I lost my penny,” I said. “You
lost your penny? But what made you come up here and hide?”
If my father hadn’t been there, I might have told her. But when I looked up at my father,
it was like daylight tearing the memory of a foolish dream. How could I bear the shame of
repeating before him the soft twisting visions I had built in my head as I buried the penny
and dug it up again? How could I explain that pit-of-the-stomach sickness which struck
through the whole day when I had to believe, at last, that it was really lost? How could I
explain that I wasn’t really hiding from them? That the only possible place to run from that
awful feeling of loss was the soft, dark safeness of bed? That I had cried myself asleep?
(A) “I lost my penny,” I said. I looked at father and turned my face into the pillow. “I want
to go to sleep.”
“Danny,” my mother said, “it’s almost nine o’clock. You haven’t had a bite of supper. Do
you know you almost scared the life out of us!”
“You better get some supper,” my father said. It was the only time he had spoken.
I never dreamed of father ever mentioning it again. But the next morning when we had
the forks in our hands, he seemed to hold up the moment of actually leaving for the field.
“Don’t you have any idea where you lost your penny?” he said suddenly.
“Yes,”  I said,  “I know just about.”
We walked down the road together. He didn’t hold my hand.  “It’s right here
somewheres,” I said. “I was playing with it in the dust.” He looked at me, questioningly but
he didn’t ask me what game anyone could possibly play with a penny in the dust. He got

down on his knees and drew his fingers carefully through the dust, like a harrow. He found
the penny almost at once. He held it in his hand, as if the moment of passing it to me were
a deadline for something he dreaded to say, but must.
“Dan,” he said, “You needn’t have hidden. I wouldn’t have beaten you.”
“Beat me? Oh, Father! You didn’t think that was the reason ... ?” I felt almost sick. I had
to tell him the truth, no matter how foolish it was, to scatter that awful idea out of his head.
“I wasn’t hiding, Father,” I said, “I was burying my penny and pretending I was digging
up treasure. I was pretending I was finding gold. I didn’t know what to do when I lost it.”
His head was bent forward, like mere listening.
“I was pretending it was gold,” I said desperately, “and I was pretending I bought you
a mowing machine so you could get your work done early every day so you and I could go
into town in the big automobile I pretended I bought and everyone would turn around and
look at us driving down the streets.”
His head was perfectly still and then he looked up. It was the only time I had ever seen
tears in his eyes. I wondered, though, why he hesitated and then put the penny back in
his own pocket.
Yesterday I knew. I never found any fortune and we never had a car to ride in together.
But I think he knew what that would be like, just the same. (B) I found the penny again
yesterday, when we were getting out his good clothes — in an upper vest pocket where
no one ever carries change. It was still shining. He must have kept it polished. I left it there.

논술형

In Armenia, by tradition, and especially in the rural areas, a woman needs to wait for the
man to offer his hand for the handshake. Between good friends and family members, a
kiss on the cheek and a light hug are also common.
A full list would be extensive, as each country differs just a little bit in the way people
greet each other. To add to the hapless traveler’s confusion are the different hand
gestures around the world. Before visiting a foreign country, it is recommended to check
on the various meanings of hand gestures, as a visitor may unknowingly find himself in a
very unpleasant situation. Here is why:
Waving your full arm side to side in many countries is recognized as saying “hello” or
“goodbye”. However, in East Asian countries  it is considered overly demonstrative.
Additionally in some European countries, as well as Japan and Latin America, it can be
confused for a “no” or general negative response. In India, it means “come here.”
Counting with fingers starting with index finger toward the pinkie can make people
confused in Germany and Austria as forefinger held up means two instead of one,
especially when ordering a round of drinks. In Japan, the thumb alone means five. When
Hungarians count on their hand, they start with the thumb being number one.
Curling the index finger, or four fingers toward you as a gesture of inviting somebody to
come closer, can be mistaken for “good bye” in southern Europe. In the Philippines and
East Asia, curling the index finger is used only to beckon dogs.
Pointing directly to someone or something using index finger in Europe is considered
impolite. In China, Japan, Latin America and Indonesia it has very rude connotations. In
many African countries, the index finger is used for pointing only at inanimate objects.
Gestures can say more than words, and just as we are usually very careful when using
foreign languages, we should consider carefully what hand gestures we should display
whilst in different cultures. The world is indeed full of diversities, so enjoy your learning.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.[12점]
It is a slow day in town and the streets are deserted. Times are tough, everybody is in
debt, and everybody is living on credit.
A tourist visiting the area drives through town, stops at the hotel, and lays a $100 bill on
the desk saying he wants to inspect the rooms upstairs to pick one for the night.
As soon as he walks upstairs, the hotel owner grabs the bill and runs next door to pay his
debt to the butcher. The butcher takes the $100 and runs down the street to repay his
debt to the pig farmer. The pig farmer takes the $100 and heads off to pay his bill to his
supplier, the Co-op. The guy at the Co-op takes the $100 and runs to the hotel and pays
off his restaurant bill to the hotel owner.
The hotel owner then places the $100 back on the counter so the traveler will not
suspect anything. At that moment the traveler comes down the stairs, states that the
rooms are not satisfactory, picks up the $100 and leaves.
No one produced anything. No one earned anything. However, the whole town is now out of
debt and looks to the future with a lot more optimism.

A stimulus package is a package of economic measures that a government uses to
stimulate a floundering economy. The objective of a stimulus package is to increase
spending and investment by injecting money into the economy through measures like
financial aid or tax cuts. Direct payments give people more money to spend, boosting
demand  for goods and  services. Tax cuts reduce  financial burdens, encouraging
businesses to invest and hire more workers. Government spending on projects like
infrastructure creates jobs and stimulates various industries. This policy helps reduce
debts, create liquidity, and stimulate demand.

The scene was the night when he had asked her to come up on his pedestal with him and
share his greatness. He could not, now, for the pain of it, allow his mind to dwell upon
thememory of her great beauty that night—the careless wave of her hair, the tenderness

But, alas! The incense of her admiration had been so sweet and praising. He allowed the
inference to pass without denial. Without protest, he allowed her to place on his head (A)
this false laurel of Spanish scholarship. He let it grace his conquering head, and, among its
soft twisted branches, he did not feel (B) the sharp thorn that would pierce him later.
How glad, how shy, how quivering she was! How she fluttered like a caught bird when
he laid his greatness at her feet! He could have sworn, and he could swear now, that
unmistakable consent was in her eyes, but she would give him no direct answer. “I will
send you my answer tomorrow,” she said, and he, the spoiled, confident winner, smilingly
granted the delay. The next day he waited, impatient, in his rooms for the word. At noon
her servant came to the door to deliver the strange cactus in the red earthen jar. There
was no note, no message, merely a tag upon the plant bearing a foreign or botanical
name. He waited until night, but her answer did not come. His large pride and hurt vanity
kept him from seeking her. Two evenings later they met at a dinner. Their greetings were
conventional, but she looked at him, breathless, wondering, and eager. He was polite and
waited for her explanation. With womanly swiftness she took her cue from his manner
and turned to snow and ice. Thus, since then, they had drawn apart. What did he do
wrong? Who had been to blame? Humbled now, he sought the answer in the ruins of his
conceit. If…
The voice of the other man in the room, complaining, cut through his thoughts to bring him
back to consciousness.
“Hey, Trysdale, what the hell is the matter with you? You look unhappy as if you yourself

논술형

Art Beyond Sight and Sound
For most people, going to concerts and museums is a way to experience a world apart
from the routine of ordinary, everyday life. For some, however, such chances are limited.
The visually impaired, for instance, face major challenges when  it comes to viewing
artwork in a museum. Likewise, for those with hearing difficulties, listening to music
becomes less an attempt at absorbing the rhythm and flow than a struggle to grasp even a
single note.
In the world of art, a number of renowned international institutions are putting more effort
into making artwork more accessible for those with limited vision. In stark contrast to the
usual “no-touching”  policy,  several  institutions have held  exhibitions  or introduced
programs that challenge the stereotypical notion that the blind cannot “see” and therefore
cannot appreciate art. The Prado, for instance, one of the most prestigious art institutions in
Spain, has held its first ever exhibition for the blind.
Out of the vast range of priceless paintings, six works by Spanish masters, such as
Francisco Goya and Diego Velázquez, were reproduced for the special audience eager to lay
their hands on the pieces. The pioneering exhibition was embraced enthusiastically for
being the first of its kind to introduce relief painting techniques that add volume and texture
to paintings, thereby allowing the blind to create mental images of the works by touching
them. The copies in the Prado exhibition have the same proportions as the originals but are
slightly smaller to allow the blind guests to touch and feel their way through the entire
surface and see the work with their mind’s eye.
(중략)
On another front, attempts at opening up the world of music to children with hearing
problems are being carried out across Europe. One special project has examined the way
Beethoven’s own deafness not only brought him to despair but greatly influenced his
compositions. Obsessed with being able to feel the vibrations of the piano upon losing his
hearing, Beethoven utilized trills, extreme registers, and long stretches of pedal to create
huge vibrations of sound, and it is thought that these techniques make his music more
Ⅹ. 심화 영어 독해와 작문 성취수준
accessible to those with impaired hearing.
The project’s aims are to illustrate that deafness is no barrier to making or appreciating
music and to show that music can be appreciated in many different ways—through
vibrations, gestures, body movements, rhythms, and by reading music on the printed page.
This project invites children to an orchestral hall so that they can feel instruments being
played, for example by resting their arms on the strings of a piano to feel the vibrations
caused by a hammer striking a string when a key is pressed.
(중략)
Programs like these are valuable in that not only do they overturn the stereotypes and
assumptions we have about the visually and aurally challenged, but they also force us to
rethink the way we ourselves perceive art. By foregrounding the hidden aspects of statues
and symphonies, such programs show that our own perceptions are often confined by the
limitations of our presumptively perfect senses.

How Different Cultures Understand Time
Some people exaggerate cultural differences, sometimes oversimplifying the matter into a
false divide between Eastern and Western cultures. But in everyday life, differences do
exist, and sometimes these differences cause friction between people from different
cultures or countries. Time is one thing that is understood in different ways from one
culture to another, and there are at least three distinct ways in which people perceive its
flow. Let’s have a look.
Linear Time
The linear view of time is common to profit-driven societies, which view time as a
precious, even scarce commodity—as Benjamin Franklin famously put it, time is money!
According to this view, time is always flowing quickly by, and once it has passed, it is
irreversibly gone. So if you want to make the most of time, you had better move fast to keep
up with it. Because of this, people with a linear view of time cannot bear to be idle. In linear
time, the past is over, but you can seize the present and make it work for you in the
immediate future.
According to linear time, time is being wasted when decisions are not being made or
actions are not being performed. People who adopt a linear view of time also tend to be
monochronic; that is, they prefer to do only one thing at a time, to concentrate on it, and to
do it within a fixed schedule. They think that in this way they get more things done and that
they do them more efficiently. They also equate working time with success: the harder you
work—the more hours, that is—the more successful you will be and the more money you
will make. If you have 40 years of earning capacity and you want to make $4 million, that
means you need to earn $100,000 per year. If you can achieve this in 250 working days, that
comes to $400 a day or $50 an hour. Thus, those who orient themselves towards time in
this way might say that their time costs $50 an hour.
Flexible Time
Flexible time is quite different from linear time. People who view time as flexible readily
adjust deadlines, and they tend to do many things all at once, often in an unplanned order.
The more things they can do at the same time, the happier and the more fulfilled they feel.
Ⅹ. 심화 영어 독해와 작문 성취수준
Therefore, they organize their time and their lives in an entirely different way from those
who adhere to linear time. For these people, the best way to invest one’s time is in human
interaction, because nurturing one’s relationships with others is far more important than
being punctual and sticking to strict schedules.
Of course, those who subscribe to flexible time may go through the motions of observing
schedules and deadlines, especially if a linear-active partner or colleague insists on it, but in
the end they consider the present reality to be more important than future appointments.
Priority is given to the relative thrill or significance of each task or meeting, and the passing
of time will be ignored if it means that conversations will be left unfinished.
For those following linear time, time is clock- and calendar-related, divided for their
convenience, measurement, and disposal; it is an objective truth that dictates one’s actions.
On the other hand, for those living in the world of flexible time, time is subjective and
event-related; it can be shaped, stretched, or manipulated, regardless of what the clock
says. Those who have a linear perspective on time might say, “I have to rush. My time is
almost up!” People living in flexible time, however, would scorn this submissive attitude to
schedules. They would only use this expression if they were close to death.

2. People with a linear perspective on time and those with a flexible perspective prioritize
tasks and schedules in very different ways, but they both aim to manage their time
effectively. People with a linear view focus on strict schedules and prefer to complete
one task at a time, believing this is the most efficient way to work. In contrast, people
with a flexible view often handle many tasks at once and adjust their schedules
depending on the situation, placing greater importance on human relationships than
deadlines. Both perspectives try to make the best use of time, but linear time relies
on structure, while flexible time values adaptability.

Walk, Don’t Run, Your Way to a Healthy Heart
In fact, walking quickly can lower your risk of high blood pressure, high cholesterol,
and diabetes as much as running, according to a new study conducted at Lawrence
Berkeley National Laboratory,  Life Science Division  in Berkley,  Calif.  All three
conditions are risk factors for heart disease and stroke and you can do something
about them.
Researchers analyzed runners in the National Runners’ Health Study and walkers
in the National Walkers’ Health Study. They found that the same energy used for
moderate-intensity  walking and  vigorous-intensity  running  resulted  in  similar
reductions in risk for high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, and possibly
heart disease over many years. The more people walked or ran each week, the more
their health benefits increased.
All you have to do is lace up with a good pair of sneakers - and walk. It’s that
easy. It’s also safe, the least expensive and has the lowest dropout rate of any type
of exercise. “It’s not a skill-dependent form of activity,” Pate said. “It’s the most
accessible form of physical activity. You can do it almost anywhere. And it doesn’t
require a lot of equipment.” Before you know it, quick walking can become a part
of your daily routine. And you’ll obtain plenty of benefits. “Clearly, walking is an
important form of physical activity,” Pate said.

Walk or Run: A Simple Path to a Healthy Heart
Walking quickly can improve your heart health just as much as running, according
to a study by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Researchers studied over 48,000
participants in the National Runners’ and Walkers’ Health Studies for six years. They
found that both moderate-intensity walking and vigorous-intensity running, when
using the same amount of energy, helped reduce the risks of high blood pressure,
high cholesterol, and diabetes. These are all key factors that can lead to heart disease.

Walking is easy, affordable, and gentle on the body, making  it a great option for
everyone. You can fit walking into your day by breaking it into 10–15-minute sessions,
taking the stairs, or walking your dog. The American Heart Association says that
walking for 30 minutes a day can lower the risk of heart disease by 30–40%.
For some people, running may be a better choice if they want to burn more calories
or improve endurance faster. However, both activities are excellent for staying fit and
healthy. The best option depends on your fitness level and health goals.
Walking is one of the simplest ways to stay active. All you need is a good pair of
sneakers and a bit of time. Start walking today, and you’ll soon enjoy the benefits of
a healthier heart and a more energetic life.

“It is approaching one in the morning, and I am glued to my phone. The TV is on, the laptop
is whirring away, and I have even got the radio on standby. If anyone asked, I would tell
them I am a night person. The truth, though, is that I am suffering from FOMO, a condition
whose acronymic name stands for the Fear of Missing Out.”
This is the experience of worrying that other people have more friends than you, are doing
more interesting things than you, and are just all around living a better and cooler life. It is
actually not something new—diverse forms of this condition have been around for ages. Yet
its prevalence and intensity in our modern age are unprecedented.
One of the prime sources of FOMO, as you may have guessed, is social media, which allows
you to check out what is happening in other people’s lives. Imagine you are spending a quiet
night at home and you see pictures online of your friends having fun together. Or maybe
you are still toiling away at your homework and you catch some of your fellow classmates
enjoying their day out at the amusement park.
Just scroll through the mountains of pictures and comments on social media and you will
get the idea. However, FOMO-inducing media is hardly limited to the Internet. Simply take
a look at the TV and you are faced with reality shows that tend to glorify the fabulous
lifestyles of the rich and famous and advertisements that are populated only by gorgeous
young people at beach parties or on fantastic road trips.
What might be some of your first reactions to such visual stimuli? The symptoms of an
onset of FOMO include nervousness, sudden restlessness, and a general feeling of anxiety
that starts to impair your brain function. Allowed to fester, it sucks you into living and
judging other people’s lives instead of enjoying your own, and  it turns what could be
motivation for taking life by the horns into extreme envy and depression. In order to remedy
the situation once you feel an attack of FOMO coming on, make efforts to ward it off by
asking yourself the following simple questions.

Is this an accurate representation of reality?
Nobody is gullible enough to accept everything at face value. Almost everyone intrinsically
knows that what is shown on social media and TV is not an accurate representation of
people’s real lives. What people post on social media is what they want others to see and
shows how they wish to see themselves. Only the most positive aspects of their lives are
set in the limelight, while the negative, neutral, and mundane are deliberately edited out.
What is more, in our age of photoshop, the images themselves are highly edited and
sanitized. So why should you develop negative feelings about yourself based on inaccurate
representations of reality?

예시 답안
1. FOMO, or the Fear of Missing Out, means feeling worried that other people have more
exciting and better lives than you. In today’s world, FOMO has become very common
because of social media and TV. It can cause nervousness, restlessness, and anxiety,
which make  it hard to focus or think clearly. Over time, FOMO can make people
compare their lives to others, feel unhappy, and even lead to envy and depression.
2. Content creators, influencers, and media platforms can help reduce FOMO by showing
real and balanced  lives instead  of  perfect and  unrealistic images. For example,
influencers can share normal, everyday moments, not just their best highlights. Media
platforms can also create campaigns that show different and honest life experiences.
These efforts can help people understand that what they see online or on TV is not
real life, making them feel less anxious or unhappy about their own lives. This way,
they can focus more on enjoying their own reality.

systems and argue over their results. “Fundamentally, we’re interested in considering the
ethical and social impact of such systems,” says Alan Winfield, professor of electronic
engineering at the University of the West of England. It is time, he says, to make some crucial
decisions. “If we get it wrong, there will be consequences.” It is a point well illustrated by
IBM’s intelligent computer system Watson. Two years after beating human contestants at
the quiz show Jeopardy!, Watson has turned to medical school and could soon be diagnosing
diseases.
In 2013, commercial products utilizing Watson’s ability to process medical information and
make decisions were developed for clinical use. With access to the latest developments as
well as the medical records of patients, systems such as Watson could suggest an accurate
diagnosis faster and more often. But there is a problem. With intelligent systems accessing
medical records comes the fear of compromised privacy and security, as many of these
intelligent systems will be connected via the Internet. Should we allow an intelligent system
access to our personal medical records? According to Tony Prescott, professor of cognitive
neuroscience at the University of Sheffield, “It is a decision we have to make as a society:
whether we want to give up some of our privacy in order to get improved services like
better healthcare.” It is an issue that boils down to trust, making it essential that doctors are
closely involved in training such systems, understanding how they work, and confirming
that the diagnoses are spot on.
(중략)
When technology develops,  it develops very quickly.  “It  is moving way faster than
legislation and yes, it’s a problem,” says Tony Belpaeme, professor of cognitive systems
and robotics at the University of Plymouth. And the issues are international. “The trouble is
that your data is now spread globally and legislation isn’t the same across various regions
Ⅹ. 심화 영어 독해와 작문 성취수준
across the planet,” says Belpaeme. With recent revelations over the access and use of data
by various government agencies still in people’s minds, issues of data storage, privacy, and
security need to be aired openly. With the possibility of technology becoming intertwined
with our very bodies, the threat of unauthorized access is inevitable.
We do not have to go so far as to worry that “full artificial intelligence could spell the end of
the human race,” as Stephen Hawking has told the BBC. AI will not lead us to doomsday. It
has enormous potential benefits—the potential to cure all diseases, eliminate poverty, and
help life spread into outer space. But it is also clear that our contemplation of its effects
should keep pace with the rapid development of AI itself. Let’s not just start this voyage
without a map. We should carefully plan the course that lies ahead.

The Job Market Is Going Green
If you are thinking about your career path, you have probably heard that there are
white-collar workers, such as lawyers, sales managers, and bankers, who sit behind office
desks, and blue-collar workers, such as mechanics, electricians, and construction workers,
who practice their trade in factories or on building sites. But have you noticed that another
“collar” group has emerged in the job market? In fact, a great number of workers are trading
in their white and blue collars for one of a more verdant hue. These new green-collar jobs
can range from manual to managerial, so they are not quite as easily defined as white-collar
or blue-collar ones, but they all have the common goal of improving the quality of our
environment by reducing waste and pollution.
Ⅹ. 심화 영어 독해와 작문 성취수준
2. 다음 글을 읽고 green-collar job의 정의를 찾아 쓰세요. 1번에서 추측했던 정의와 어떻게 다른지
확인하세요. [2점]
Whether a job is green collar or not can also sometimes be fuzzy because some
companies are involved  in making both  traditional and environmentally  friendly
products. For example, think about people who work in a mill that produces steel
for both big SUVs and wind turbines. Are they blue-collar or green-collar workers?
Do the lawyers who work for a biodiesel company have white-collar or green-collar
jobs? The answers depend on how you look at the job and  its responsibilities.
According to a report commissioned by the United Nations Environment Programme,
green-collar jobs are those that contribute to the protection of biodiversity; the
reduction of the consumption of energy, materials, and water; the de-carbonization
of the environment; and the minimization of waste.

A green-collar job’s tint varies with how sophisticated the skills that  it requires
are. Some jobs requiring manual skills are referred to as “dark green” jobs. They are
for those who are looking for a secure future and want to work on the nuts and
bolts of that future. Dark green jobs, such as bolting down solar panels or operating
a spray foam machine, are ideal for people with relatively limited education and skills,
because they can get training from a combination of “learn as you earn” experience
on the job and formal classroom or online study. Other green-collar jobs are
managerial or scientific and may involve designing energy-efficient buildings or
planning out green space for a city. These “light green” jobs may be suitable for
those who are not up for the demands of dark green jobs. One of the benefits of

better opportunities by adding “green” to their skill set. For example, if an accountant
learns how to manage corporate carbon offsets, this specialized skill could potentially
help him or her transition to a more promising position with higher remuneration.
With the growing threat of global warming and the devastation of our environment,
“green” has been a way to enter the business landscape around the world. One of
the most promising sectors of the green economy is renewables. “Renewables are
poised to tackle our energy crisis and create millions of new jobs across the world,”
says Worldwatch senior researcher Michael Renner. “Meanwhile, fossil fuel jobs are
increasingly becoming fossils themselves.”

1. 다음 글을 읽고 질문에 답하세요.[5점]
Another way to convey or evoke feelings is by intentionally (or unintentionally) choosing certain
sentence patterns. Imagine several protesters were injured at a demonstration when the police
were trying to disperse the crowd. If the reporter has bad feelings about what the police did, the
headline may read “Police wound three civilians.” If, on the other hand, the reporter feels that
protesters were more responsible for their injuries, the headline might instead read “Three
civilians are wounded.” By manipulating sentence patterns, that is, by hiding or revealing the
person who caused the injuries, the reporter can express his or her personal feelings and try to
evoke the same feelings in the readers.
Politicians, advertisers, and reporters are not the only people who manipulate feelings through
language. Ordinary people make clever use of word choices to express their feelings, too. We all
know that language allows us several ways of saying the same thing, and that even synonyms
differ in connotation, the associated meanings of words. Different words can evoke different
feelings because their connotations can be either positive or negative.
For example, when some children are playing in the next room, one person might say, “Listen to

those little ones,” but another might say, “Listen to those brats.” The terms “little ones” and “brats”
refer to the same children, but they tell us something about the feelings of the speakers. The first
person probably thinks the kids are really sweet, while the second one clearly thinks they are
being annoying. The two expressions have the same basic factual meaning but very different
connotations. The first one has a positive connotation, whereas the other carries a negative
connotation. If someone prefers to avoid expressing strong feelings in this situation, the speaker can
choose to say, “Listen to those children,” because “children” is a neutral word.
The fact that words and expressions carry connotations is one reason why we have to be very
careful when we read the news. We should always be on guard because reporters may be trying
to transfer their emotions to us. For example, while covering the same event, the headline in one
newspaper reads “Terrorists move south,” while in another it reads “Freedom fighters move
south.” You can guess from their choice of words which side each newspaper is on.

more, starting school later could cause problems.  It might make after-school activities
harder to do. Parents might have trouble getting to work on time  if they need to drop

school times, we should focus on going to bed earlier and having better sleep habits.

Sample Dialogue

B: That’s too bad. What do you do when you feel stressed out?
A: Personally, I watch movies when I feel stressed out.

A: Absolutely. Watching movies helps me escape from worries.
B: That sounds great. I'd like to give it a try.

[Script]
When you work towards something greater than yourself, you find meaning, you find
purpose. So the question I hope you will carry forward from here is: How will you serve
humanity? At MIT, you've learned how much power science and technology have to
change the world for the better. Thanks to discoveries made right here, billions of people
are leading healthier, more productive, more fulfilling lives. If we are ever going to solve
some of the hardest problems still facing the world today—everything from cancer to
climate change to educational inequality—then technology  will help us do  it. But
technology alone isn’t the solution. Sometimes, it’s even part of the problem.
Last year, I had the chance to meet with Pope Francis. This is a man who has spent more
time comforting the afflicted in slums than he has with heads of state. He knew an
unbelievable amount about technology. It was obvious to me that he had thought deeply
about its opportunities, its risks, its morality. Never has humanity had such power over
itself, yet nothing ensures that it will be used wisely.
Technology today is integral to almost all aspects of our lives, and most of the time, it’s a
force for good. And yet, the potential adverse consequences are spreading faster and
cutting deeper than ever before—threats to our security, threats to our privacy, fake
news, and social media that becomes anti-social. Sometimes, the very technology that is
meant to connect us divides us. Technology is capable of doing great things, but  it
doesn’t want to do great things. It doesn’t want anything. That part takes all of us. It takes
our values, our commitment to our families, our neighbors, and our communities. It takes
our love of beauty and our belief that all of our fates are interconnected. It takes our
decency, our kindness.
I’m not worried about artificial intelligence giving computers the ability to think like
humans. I’m more concerned about people thinking like computers—without values or
compassion, without concern for consequences. That is what we need you to help us
guard against. If science is a search in the darkness, then the humanities are a candle that
shows us where we've been and the dangers that  lie ahead. As Steve once said,
technology alone is not enough. It is technology married with the liberal arts, married with
the humanities, that makes our hearts sing. When you keep people at the center of what
you do, it can have an enormous impact.

능력과 창의적 표현 능력을 평가하기 위한 논술형 문항이다.
•        성취수준 A에 속하는 학생들이 수행할 수 있는 문항으로, 신화의 문화적 중요성을 탐구하거나
이를 현대적 맥락과 연결하는 등의 문항으로 확장할 수 있으며, 성취수준 B 혹은 C에 해당하는
학생의 경우, Step 1,2를 1, 2차시로 나누어 활동 시간을 넉넉히 부여하며, 탬플릿을 제공하고,
성취수준 D, E에 속하는 학생들에게는 세부적인 지침이나 작성 템플릿을 구체화하여 제공한다.
•         미디어 도구를 사용하여 효과적으로 협업하는 학생들의 능력을 평가한다. 예를 들어, 개인의 기여개발 방향 및
도를 기록할 수 있는 협업 도구(Google Docs/Slides: 편집 및 추가 내용을 기록, Padlet: 개별 활용 시         기여도를 시각적으로 보여줌)를 사용하면 각 학생의 작업 기록을 검토하여 개별 기여도를 평가할
고려 사항        수 있다.
•        다양한 학습 스타일을 수용할 수 있도록 미디어 도구 및 협업 방법의 유연성이 필요하다. 협업
과정을 교사가 관찰하거나, 교사가 퀴즈를 설계하여 학생의 응답을 통해 이해도와 참여도를 파악
할 수 있고, 또는 학생들에게 구체적인 역할(예: 연구자, 작가, 발표자, 편집자)을 배정하여 협업
정도를 확인할 수 있다. 학생은 협업 과정에서 자신의 역할에 대해 개인별 성찰기록문을 작성할
수 있다.
•        협업 및 글쓰기 과정에서 개선이 필요한 강점과 영역을 파악하기 위해 연습 기회를 충분히
제공하고, 성찰과 피드백의 단계를 가진다.

Discussion 1:Why Did Pandora Open the Box?
A: Pandora opened the box because she was curious. Even though she was told not to
open it, she couldn’t resist the temptation to find out what was inside. This shows how
curiosity is a natural part of being human. Sometimes, people make decisions based
on their curiosity, even when they know it might cause problems. Her action reflects
how humans often take risks to learn or discover new things.
Discussion 2: Consequences of Pandora’s Actions
A: When Pandora opened the box, many troubles came out, such as sadness, disease,
greed, and death. These things made life harder for people and ended the peaceful
world they once had. However, hope was left inside the box. Hope gave people the
strength to keep going, even when life became difficult. This shows that even in hard
times, there is always something positive to help us move forward.
Discussion 3: Lessons and Modern Implications of Mythology
A: This myth teaches us to think carefully about the choices we make because our actions
can have big consequences. It also shows that even when bad things happen, hope
can help us overcome them. In modern life, this lesson can apply to problems like new
technologies. For example, while smartphones and AI make our lives easier, they can
also create problems like stress or privacy concerns. This myth reminds us to be careful
and find a good balance when we face new challenges and situations.

At the bottom of the box, Pandora found a small, shining light. It was hope. Unlike the
evils, hope felt warm and gentle. Pandora realized that hope was meant to help people
deal with the troubles she had released.
In today’s world, hope  still helps people face big problems. For example, with the
environmental crisis, hope gives people the courage to try new ideas, like using clean
energy and planting trees. Hope is not about waiting for things to get better; it’s about
believing in change and working hard to make  it happen.

together to solve problems and create a better future.

At the bottom of the box, Pandora saw a faint glow. It was hope. Confused, she turned
to Prometheus, who had been watching from afar.
“Why is hope in the box?” Pandora asked. Prometheus smiled gently and said, “I placed
it there to help humanity. Even when life becomes difficult, hope will give them the
strength to keep going.”

[Step 3] Screenplay: "The Magic Mirror"
Scene 1: The Discovery
(The main character is in their room, standing in front of an old, dusty mirror that suddenly
starts glowing.)
Main character: (Startled) What on earth? Did someone sneak something into my room?
Why is this mirror glowing?
Mirror: (In a calm, mysterious voice) Good evening. I am your magic mirror, here to guide
you on a journey.
Main character: (In disbelief) A talking mirror? This has to be a dream. What do you mean,
"guide me"?
Mirror: (Gently) I can tell you one secret about your future, but only if you listen carefully.
Are you ready to know?
Scene 2: The Advice
(The main character hesitates but eventually leans closer to the mirror.)
Main character: (Curious) Okay, fine. Tell me. What is this secret?
Mirror: You will achieve something remarkable soon, but only if you take the time to help
someone in need today.
Main character: (Frowning) That’s vague… But fine,  I’ll give  it a shot.
(The main character grabs a backpack and heads out of the room.)

announcement.)

our school in the regional debate competition! Your hard work and dedication have
truly paid off.
Main character: (To themselves, shocked) Wait… Could this be what the mirror meant?
Scene 5: Reflection
(That evening, the main character stands in front of the mirror again.)

remember: your actions shape your future.
Main character: (Nods)  I guess  I’ll be seeing more of you, then.

선다형
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
As a young American teaching English in China, Joe would walk to the cafeteria each day at
lunch time. He was teaching at a medical school and often saw the same elderly doctor
coming from the other direction. She always greeted him with, “Have you eaten yet?” Joe,
who only knew a little Chinese, would reply, “No, no,” pointing to his empty rice bowl and
chopsticks. Joe thought it seemed obvious that he hadn’t eaten yet—he was just heading to
the cafeteria! He found it very strange that she asked the same question every day and
thought, “She doesn’t seem to pay attention to details.”
After a few weeks, someone finally explained to Joe that “Have you eaten yet?” is just a
polite greeting, not a literal question. Food is such a key part of Chinese culture that this
phrase is a way of showing care for someone’s well-being. Joe had understood the literal
meaning of the Chinese language, but he did not grasp the _________________________.
① humor in the greeting
② proper grammar of the phrase
③ emotional tone of the question
④ cultural intent behind the words
⑤ value of being polite to elderly people
출처: Person Longman, Tips for Teaching Culture (Ann C. Wintergerst 외, 2011), p.13
정답 해설
위 상황에서 오해가 발생한 원인을 정확히 이해했는지를 묻는 문항이다. 조(Joe)는 “Have you eaten
yet?”의 뜻을 지닌 중국어 문장의 문자 그대로의 뜻(literal meaning)은 이해했지만 그 말이 담고 있는
문화적 의미나 의도(“showing care for someone’s well-being”)를 이해하지 못했기 때문에 빈 칸에
들어갈 말은 “④ cultural intent behind the words”가 된다.

Funerals around the world show how cultures honor and remember the dead. While people in
different cultures all mourn for their loved ones, the ways they do it are different.
In South Korea, funerals are family-centered and typically
involve the burial of a coffin or cremation*. Attendees are
expected to wear black as a sign of respect, and while they
may share a meal in the funeral hall, toasting is not allowed as
it is considered inappropriate during a time of mourning.
In  Ghana,  the  families
provide food, drinks, music, and dance, making the event
celebratory. Attendees are usually dressed in black or black
and red traditional funeral clothing. A unique part of Ghanaian
funerals is the use of colorful fantasy coffins, which are
custom-made to represent the deceased’s* job or interests. For example, a fisherman might
have a fish-shaped coffin. Many people in Ghana believe that a showy funeral can raise a
person's status in the next life.
At a Tibetan funeral, the family wears white while the
attendees should wear black or dark clothing. Their practices
are based on Buddhist teachings about reincarnation*, which
sees death as a transition rather than an end. A common
practice  is sky  burial, where the body  is placed on a
mountaintop for birds to eat. Family members do not watch the process because it is a holy
ceremony.                                                                        *cremation: 화장
*the deceased: 고인
*reincarnation: 윤회, 환생

(A) The Korean language has different levels of politeness, and you choose your words
based on who you’re talking to. For example, when talking to adults, teachers, or
someone you don’t know well, you use  polite endings  like -요  (yo) or -습니다
(seum-ni-da). For example, instead of saying “고마워” (go-ma-weo) to mean “thank
you,” you would say “감사합니다” (gam-sa-ham-ni-da) to sound more polite.
(B) One way to sound more polite and respectful when speaking in English is by using
modal verbs, such as would, could and might. These verbs are often used in formal
speech to make requests or suggestions sound more polite. Adding a modal verb to a
sentence softens your tone, making your opinion feel less direct and strong, which
encourages the other person to listen more openly. For example, instead of saying, “I
want coffee,” you could say, “I would like to have coffee.” When in doubt, using a modal
verb is a helpful way to make any question or statement sound more polite.
(C) In Finnish, politeness is often expressed through tone, word choice, and indirectness
rather than special grammar forms. Finnish doesn’t have formal and informal pronouns
like many other languages, but respect is shown by speaking calmly and avoiding overly
direct language. For example, instead of saying “Give me the book,” a polite Finnish
speaker might say Voisitko antaa minulle kirjan? (“Could you give me the book?”), using
the conditional form voisitko to soften the request. Additionally, saying kiitos (“thank
you”) often and maintaining a respectful tone are key ways to show politeness in
Finnish.

Beliefs about numbers often have a basis in science and nature. For instance, early
astrologers believed that seven planets governed the universe, including human lives. A
seventh child was thought to possess special powers, and those born in a year divisible
by seven were considered lucky. For Pythagoras, three was the perfect number
symbolizing harmony, wisdom, and understanding. There is even a Latin phrase meaning
every set of three is complete. The same number can carry different meanings in
different cultures. In Egypt, five is a lucky number that represents the universe. In
contrast, the Ashanti people in Ghana consider five to be an unlucky number. While the
ancient Greeks, particularly the Pythagoreans — who saw it as the source of the perfect
tetractys (1+2+3+4=10) — viewed four as a perfect and practical number, it carries a very
different connotation in parts of Asia. Specifically, in China, four is considered unlucky
due to its similar pronunciation to “death” (“four” as “sì” and “death” as “sǐ”).

Banknote Character Selection
Banknotes are money, but they are also little artworks in our pockets. They can be a
symbol of identity and nationhood and, as such, designs are constantly evolving over time.
Across the world, banknote designs commonly incorporate people, iconic landscapes,
buildings and nature.
Images of monarchs have been used on UK coinage for hundreds of years but have only
been a key part of the design of Bank of England banknotes over the past 60 years. Her
Majesty Queen Elizabeth II became the first monarch to appear on a banknote in 1960. And
since 1970, Bank of England banknotes have also featured important historical characters
on the reverse side.
Traditionally, the Governor of the Bank of England has decided which characters appear on
new banknotes. In 2015, we used a new character selection process for the first time for
our latest £20 banknote, asking the public to nominate the visual artist they wanted to see
on the design. The Banknote Character Advisory Committee, which includes both external
members and Bank of England staff, shortlisted a number of characters. Based on this
shortlist, the Governor of the Bank of England at the time, Mark Carney, chose the painter J
M W Turner to appear on the £20.
We invited the public to participate again in 2018 for the new £50, based on the theme of
science. There was an unprecedented response. This time, the call for public input attracted
over 225,000 nominations for 989 characters which spanned the full breadth of scientific
endeavours, from astronomy to physics, chemistry to palaeontology and mathematics to
biochemistry. From these nominations, the scientist Alan Turing was chosen as the
character on the £50 banknote.
The mission of the Bank of England is to promote the good of the UK. As we look to the
future, banknote designs will evolve in security and aesthetics. Banknotes are symbols of
UK values, so public involvement is crucial. We will continue to strive for diversity and
representation, complying with the Equality Act 2010 and considering  all protected
characteristics in future designs.

Rechta  is one of the most popular
Algerian dishes. The name originates
from the Persian word rishta, which
means "thread" and generally refers to
noodles made of wheat flour. Algerians
make the noodles by mixing wheat
flour, salt, water, and ghee (clarified
butter) together. The dish also contains
ingredients such as chopped meat,
onions,   garlic,   turnips,   potatoes,
zucchini, and Algerian spices.
Rechta looks like soft, white noodles covered in a rich, golden sauce. It smells warm and
inviting because of the spices like cinnamon and black pepper. When you take a bite, the
noodles are soft, and the sauce is full of deep, comforting flavors.
Beyond its delicious taste, rechta holds an important place in Algerian culture. Algerians
typically enjoy it on festive occasions, including weddings and Eidal-Fitr (the end of
Ramadan). It is more than just a meal—cooking and eating Rechta together shows the
importance of family and hospitality in Algerian society. The use of spices and homemade
noodles also highlights Algeria’s rich food traditions. Additionally, as Algeria is a mainly
Muslim country, rechta does not contain pork, which is considered haran(forbidden), not
halal(permissible), under Islamic dietary laws.
I feel connected to rechta because I am interested in African culture, and this dish
feels like an invitation into Algerian life.  If  I had the chance,  I would love to try
making rechta myself so that  I can experience the joy of sharing this comforting
and special dish with people  I love and care about.

Introduction to Card News Production
What is Card News?
Card news is a form of visual media where information is presented in a series of  digital
cards. Each card combines short texts with images or graphics to convey news stories or
information clearly and engagingly. This format is popular on social media and digital news
platforms because  it is easy to read and share.
Why Use Card News?
- Visual Appeal: Combines texts and images which attract more attention than texts alone.
- Easy to Digest: Breaks down complex information into manageable pieces.
- Engaging: Increases reader engagement through interactive elements.
- Shareable: Designed  for easy  sharing on  social  media,  helping  to spread  information
quickly.
Steps to Create Card News:
1) Choose a Topic: Decide what story or information you want to present.
2) Research: Gather accurate information and relevant images.
3) Write Concise Text: Keep the text short and to the point.
4) Design the Cards: Use a consistent layout and style for  all cards. Include visuals  like
photos, illustrations, or charts.
5) Edit and Review: Make sure all information is correct and the design is appealing.
6) Publish and Share: Upload your card news to the desired platform and share  it with
your audience.

개발의 이해Ⅰ성취수준





   1   주요 용어 설명



 성취기준: 학생들이 각 교과(목)의 “영역별 내용 요소(지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･

   태도)를 학습한 결과 궁극적으로 할 수 있거나 할 수 있기를 기대하는 도달점”을

  진술한 것.

 성취수준: 학생들이 각 교과목 성취기준(들)에 도달한 정도를 나타낸 것. 이러한

  도달 정도는 몇 개의 수준으로 구분하고, 각 수준에 속한 학생들이 무엇을 알고

  할 수 있는지를 기술한 것. 성취기준별 성취수준과 영역별 성취수준 등이 있음.

   - 성취기준별 성취수준: 성취기준 단위 성취수준으로, 학교급･교과목･성취기준의

   특성에 따라 3 또는 5수준으로 구분하여 진술한 것.

   - 영역별 성취수준: 영역 단위 성취수준으로, 영역 내 성취기준들을 포괄하는 전반적인

   특성을 학교급･교과목의 특성에 따라 3수준 또는 5수준으로 구분하여 진술한 것.

   - 단, 고등학교 선택과목의 경우, 교과(과목)별 내용 체계의 특성에 따라 영역 구분이

   없는 과목(국어, 영어 등)에서는 ‘영역별 성취수준’이 없음.

Ⅰ. 성취수준 개발의 이해


   3   성취기준별 성취수준 개발


가. 개발 개요

교과 교육과정의 내용 체계와 성취기준(들)을 분석하여 지식･이해, 과정･기능,

  가치･태도의 위계나 수준을 고려하여 성취기준별로 성취수준 작성

3수준 체계(A, B, C) 또는 5수준 체계(A, B, C, D, E)로 개발하되, 성취기준 내용

  요소의 복합성 정도에 따라 수준 구별



 ￭ 성취수준 구분의 원리

   - 지식의 개념 위계나 이해의 깊이를 활용하여 수준을 구분한다.
   - 과정･기능 수행 정도나 맥락과 상황 변인으로 차별화하여 수준을 구분한다.
   - 가치･태도의 내면화와 실천과 참여 등으로 수준을 구분한다.

   수준
            지식･이해          과정･기능          가치･태도

        높은   깊은   높은   문제  복잡한  다양한       넓은  적극적

   낮음
        위계   암기   전이   인식   상황   맥락   반응   적용  실천력



나. 개발 절차


 ① 영역의 내용 체계와 성취기준(들)의 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 내용 요소

  추출 및 위계 분석

 ② 영역 내 성취기준이 포함하고 있는 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 내용 요소

  수준 및 위계 분석



                                                                       7

2022 개정 교육과정에 따른 고등학교 영어과 선택과목 성취수준



   - 교과(과목)의 영역 특성에 따라 내용 체계에 제시된 ‘가치･태도’ 범주의 내용 요소가

  성취기준에서 명시적으로 드러나지 않더라도, 교육과정 취지를 살려 영역 내 성취

  수준들에서 ‘가치･태도’ 범주 관련 내용을 되도록 반영함.

 ③ 영역 내 성취기준이 포함하고 있는 내용 요소들의 복합성 등을 고려하여 3수준

  또는 5수준의 진술문 개발

   - 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 각 범주는 그 특성을 고려하여 수준을 구분하고

  이를 복합적으로 구성하여 수준을 진술함.

 ④ 성취기준별 성취수준 작성 후 각 영역 간 수준 진술 정도, 전후 학년(군)과의 능력

  진술 위계 등을 점검

   - 같은 학년(군)에서 영역 내는 물론 영역 간 성취수준의 진술 정도를 각 수준별로

  점검하여 작성함.

   - 학년(군)이 높아짐에 따라 성취수준 간의 위계가 나타나는지 점검. 다만, 교과

   및 범주 특성에 따라 학년(군)이 높아져도 동일 수준 진술이 반복적으로 나타날

   수 있음.

가. 개발 개요

교과 교육과정의 내용 체계와 성취기준(들)을 분석하여 지식･이해, 과정･기능,

  가치･태도의 위계나 수준을 고려하여 영역별로 성취수준 작성

 ① 교과 교육과정의 특성을 반영하여 개발 단위를 결정

  하여 개발할 수 있음.

   - 이때 성취기준별 성취수준들을 범주별로 단순히 연결하기보다는 앞의 ② 단계

   1   성취기준 도달 정도 예측 및 개념화 근거


 성취기준은 수업 및 평가의 근거로서의 역할을 하지만 성취기준 자체는 도달 정도에
대한 정보가 부족하여 추가적으로 성취수준에 대한 정보가 필요하다. 교사는 성취수준
에 대한 일관된 이해를 가지고 수업과 평가를 계획하고 운영해야 하는데 성취기준별
성취수준이나 영역별 성취수준은 이러한 이해와 개념화에 도움을 줄 수 있다.
 성취기준별 성취수준은 각 성취기준에 도달한 정도를 해당 교과목 평정 단계에
따라 구체화하여 제시한 것으로 성취기준별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할
수 있다. 영역별 성취수준은 해당 교과목의 영역별로 도달할 목표를 범주(지식･이해,
과정･기능, 가치･태도)에 따라 제시한 것으로 교과목 전체 수준에서 각 범주별로
도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할 수 있다.


  • 성취기준별 성취수준은 각 성취기준에 도달한 정도를 해당 교과목 평정 단계에 따라 구체화하여 제시한
  것으로 성취기준별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할 수 있음.

  • 영역별 성취수준은 해당 교과목의 영역별로 도달할 목표를 범주(지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도)에
  따라 제시한 것으로 교과목 전체 수준에서 각 범주별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할 수
  있음.

 이러한 성취수준은 수업 설계와 평가 문항 제작에서 도달 정보나 목표를 개념화할
때도 근거가 된다. 교사 간 유사한 수준에 대한 개념을 가질 수 있도록 도움을 준다.
이때 수준 구분에 대한 유연성은 열어두되, 수준에 대한 교사 간 해석의 폭을 최대한
좁혀 교육과정 범위 내에서 수업과 평가가 실행되도록 하기 위함이다. 성취수준은 국가
수준에서 해당 교과 수행의 질 관리 및 교육과정 평가(피드백 정보 해석)를 위한 기준
역할을 할 수도 있어 궁극적으로 성취수준에 대한 정보 제공 및 국가 교육과정 질
관리에 기여한다고 볼 수 있다.

이때 초등학교에서도 준거참조평가를 실시하고 있으므로, 학기별로 수업 설계 시 학기

 우선, 학생 맞춤형 수업 설계에 활용될 수 있다. 2022 개정 교육과정은 학생 개별화

위해서 학생 수준에 맞는 진단과 학습 지원이 필요하다. 이를 위해서는 학생 수준의
진단 도구 개발 및 진단 평가 시행이 필요하다. 이때 성취기준별/영역별 성취수준이
활용될 수 있다.
 둘째, 기초학력 보장 지도 및 최소 성취수준 보장지도에 활용될 수 있다. 제1차 기초

분석하여 해당 성취기준에의 도달 정도를 판단하기 위해서 어떠한 내용을 평가해야
하는지를 기준으로 작성한다. 평가 요소는 평가의 목표와 특성을 고려하여 교육과정
성취기준에서 도출하며, 학생들의 수행 정도를 판단할 수 있도록 지식, 기능, 태도와
같은 구체적인 내용으로 기술한다.

  2) 채점 기준 설정의 근거로 활용

 성취수준은 수행평가(또는 서･논술형 문항) 도구 제작 및 채점 기준 설정의 근거로
활용된다.
 채점 기준을 설정할 때에는 모든 성취수준(A~E)을 평가할 수 있도록 수행평가
과제(또는 서･논술형 문항) 및 채점 기준을 개발한다. 모든 성취수준의 학생들이
수행할 수 있는 과제로 문항을 구성할 필요가 있다.


라. 성취 결과 산출 및 보고의 근거로 활용

 성취기준별/영역별 성취수준과 이를 활용하여 개발된 학기 단위 성취수준을 토대로
학생의 성취수준을 산출한다. 분할점수 설정과 평가 시행이 완료되면 지필평가와 수행
평가 점수를 합산하여 성취율에 따라 학생의 성취도를 산출한다. 즉, 개별 학생에 대해
A~E 또는 A~C의 성취수준을 산출한다.
 이러한 성취도 산출 과정을 통한 성적 결과 보고 시, 학기 단위 성취수준과 연계하여
학생의 실제 수행 능력 진술한다. 각 성취수준에 해당하는 학생이 무엇을 알고 할 수
있는지의 교수･학습 정보를 보고한다. 개별 학생이 알고 할 수 있는 것을 기술할 때는
미리 진술한 학기 단위 성취수준을 중심으로 개별 학생의 수행 능력을 진술한다.
 이러한 정보를 학생에게 피드백한다. 피드백은 학생의 학습 상태에 대한 정보를 제공
하여 학생의 학습과 성장을 지원하는 전체적인 과정이다. 학생의 교육 목표 도달도를
확인하고 교수･학습 개선에 활용할 수도 있다. 피드백은 점수나 성취도를 알려주거나
정답 여부를 알려주는 것에서부터 학생 개별 강약점이나 추후 학습 방향, 성장 정도 등을
알려주는 등 다양한 유형이 있다.

   Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish? Such simple
   classifications as this rarely prove to be accurate. The life cycle effect suggests that major life
  events, such as leaving home, separating from parents, getting married, or having children,
  can alter people’s values and attitudes. Many individuals say they used to be more
  adventurous and drawn to liberal lifestyles during their youth but they tend to become more
  responsible after getting married and take fewer risks after having children. A case in point is
  the assessment of ` in the workplace. In the early 2000s, when this group initially entered the
   job market, they were perceived as being less committed to their companies. However, as
  they aged and got used to their roles, they began to be increasingly recognized as diligent
  workers. This illustrates that the pursuit of freedom is more characteristic of youth than of a
   specific generation, as certain attitudes and behaviors naturally develop during different life

위 글은 세대별 특성을 단순하게 구분하는 통념에 의문을 제기하며 시작한다("Do Gen Xers only care

as this rarely prove to be accurate."라고 하며 이러한 단순한 구분이 부적절함을 지적한다. 그리고
생애주기 효과(life cycle effect)라는 새로운 관점을 제시하고, 이를 두 가지 사례를 통해 뒷받침한다.
첫 번째 사례에서는 결혼과 육아로 인한 가치관 변화라는 보편적 현상을 보여주고, 두 번째 사례에서는
밀레니얼 세대의 직장 생활 변화를 통해 세대 특성보다는 생애주기가 더 중요한 요인임을 보여준다.
이 글은 기존의 통념에 의문을 제기하고, 새로운 관점을 구체적 사례를 통해 뒷받침하는 전개 방식을
사용하고 있으므로, 정답은 ⑤ questioning an assumption and supporting an alternative with
examples.이다.

   예시 답안

  Short-form  content  like  TikTok and YouTube  Shorts has a  negative impact on
concentration. It provides quick entertainment, making people get used to fast information.
As a result, their attention spans become shorter, and they struggle to focus on long-form
content like books or lectures. This is a serious problem because deep learning and critical
thinking require sustained attention. If people cannot focus for long periods of time, they
may find it hard to study, work, or solve complex problems. To solve this issue, I try to
limit my time on short-form videos and read books or long articles every day. Also,  I
practice mindfulness  exercises  like meditation  to improve my  focus. By  balancing
entertainment and deep learning, we can protect our concentration skills and think more
deeply.

                       KlaraandtheSun by Kazuo Ishiguro
      Klara is an AF (Artificial Friend), a companion robot for children. Powered by sunlight, she
    stays healthy with the Sun’s nourishment but weakens without it. At the robot store, Klara
    watched the outside world, learning how to be the best companion. One evening, she
    thought a homeless man lying still on the street had died. The next morning, when
     sunlight returned, she saw him alive, stroking his dog. Klara believed the Sun had restored
    him and placed her faith in its power.
      Josie, a fourteen-year-old girl, visited the store with her mother, Chrissie. She bonded
    with Klara and wanted to take her home, even admitting she wasn’t always healthy. Klara
    promised to face challenges with her, and Chrissie, impressed by Klara’s thoughtfulness,
    purchased her. At Josie’s home, Klara learned Josie had undergone “lifting,” a genetic
    enhancement to improve academic prospects, but it caused severe side effects. Josie’s
     illness reminded  Chrissie  of  her  late  daughter,  Sal, who  died from the same
    complications. During a city visit, Klara discovered Mr. Capaldi, a scientist, had created a
     replica of Josie’s body. He and Chrissie planned to transfer Klara’s consciousness into it if
    Josie died. While Capaldi believed the replica would fully replace Josie, Chrissie doubted
    she could truly accept it. Klara urged Chrissie to hope for Josie’s recovery, promising to
    act only if needed.
    When Josie’s health declined, Klara prayed to the Sun at the barn where it seemed to
     rest during sunsets. She asked for its healing power to save Josie, believing in its ability to
    restore life. After days of rain, sunlight returned, shining on Josie. Miraculously, she
    recovered and grew stronger.  Years later, Josie became a healthy adult and left for
     college. Klara, no longer needed, retired to the Yard for old AFs. In the Yard, she
   remembered her days with Josie.
     Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. I did everything to learn her and do what was
           best. If necessary, I could have continued Josie, but I now believe it wouldn’t have
         worked. Something would always remain beyond reach. Mr. Capaldi thought nothing
           special was inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But
                it wasn’t inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. I would have never reached
         what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.

to navigate the complexities of human emotions and relationships as Josie battles a
mysterious illness. Through Klara, Ishiguro challenges readers to question what truly makes
us human—our inner essence or the love others feel for us. Klara’s realization that Josie’s
specialness lies in the hearts of those who love her adds depth and emotional weight
to the story. Reading this book made me reflect on my own experiences with love and
connection. Overall,  it is a deeply touching and beautifully written work that inspires
reflection on emotions, dependence, and humanity.

  정답 해설

 ②번은 “~ About 300 million tons of plastic is manufactured every year, of which between
5 and 13 million tons ends up in the oceans.”에 나와 있듯이 매년 약 3억 톤의 플라스틱이 생산되
며, 그중 500만 톤에서 1,300만 톤이 바다로 유입된다. 따라서 ②번 선택지는 지문과 일치한다.

① 지난 40년간 해양 바닥에 있는 미세플라스틱의 양이 증가했다.
→ “The amount of microplastics on the surfaces of the oceans has increased significantly
   during the past four decades.”
  해양 바닥이 아니라 해양 “표면”에 있는 미세플라스틱의 양이 크게 증가했다.

③ 35,500톤의 큰 플라스틱 조각이 바다 표면에 떠 있다.
→ “One study found that about 269,000 tons of plastic remains on the surfaces of the
   oceans.”
  본문에서, 한 연구에 따르면 약 26만 9천 톤의 플라스틱이 해양 표면에 남아 있다고 하였다.

④ 심해 바닥의 미세플라스틱의 양은 해양 표면보다 세 배 더 많다.
→“Another study showed that vast quantities of microplastics are present on the deep
   sea floor, an amount about four times the amount seen on the surfaces of the oceans.”
  지문에서는 심해 바닥에는 엄청난 양의 미세플라스틱이 존재하며, 이는 해양 표면에서 발견되는 양의
  약 4배 많다고 언급하고 있다.

⑤ 플라스틱 생산량은 2050년까지 11억 톤으로 감소할 것으로 예상된다.
→ “As plastic manufacturing is expected to rise to 1.1 billion tons by the year 2050, ~ .”
  지문에서는 2050년까지 플라스틱 생산량이 증가하여 11억 톤에 이를 것으로 예상된다고 나와 있다.

   How Do Birds Navigate?
    Migratory birds can cover thousands of kilometers on their seasonal travels, often traveling
   the same course with little deviation. The secrets of their amazing navigational skills are not
    fully understood. This is because birds are believed to combine different types of senses
  when they navigate. Researchers think that birds get navigational information from the
   sun’s position, the patterns of the stars, and landmarks seen during the day. Sensing the
   earth’s magnetic field is believed to be another navigational tool. Researchers suspect that
   a specific protein in the birds eyes is sensitive to magnetism. All of these, however, are
   hypotheses that have yet to be proven.
   How Do Birds Fly without Stopping?
     In 2013, researchers presented the first evidence that migratory birds like Alpine swifts
   can fly without a break for over six months. They captured six Alpine swifts, put monitoring
   devices on them, let them go, and recaptured three of them after a year. To the researchers’
   surprise, the data gathered by the equipment indicated that the birds had most likely flown
   without landing for 200 days. Alpine swifts feed on aerial plankton so they need not land for
   food. But what about sleep? The data implied that the birds had slept during flight, but that
    this was not full recovery sleep. They may have been in a state where half of their brain
   slept while the other half remained alert. Some birds have this special ability, and it enables
  them to sleep and navigate at the same time!
    What Hazards Do Migrating Birds Encounter?
    Migratory birds are facing a growing threat from humans. Many species migrate at night
   and are attracted to the lights of tall buildings. As a result, millions die after colliding with
   such structures. Many are also killed by wind farms.
     Especially problematic is the destruction of mudflats by humans. Mudflats are important
   stop-off locations that provide food supplies critical to birds survival. The largest tidal
   mudflats on earth are the Yellow Sea mudflats in Korea and China. However, these mudflats
   are fast disappearing as humans turn them into land. This has become one of the world’s
   greatest conservation concerns for migratory birds.

  The fourth plinth in Trafalgar Square was originally planned to hold a statue of William
IV, but due to a lack of funds, it remained empty for over 150 years. In 1995, a debate
began about how to use the empty plinth, and the RSA conducted a public poll to gather

and Winnie the Pooh. However,  it was decided that the fourth plinth would be used to

  정답 해설

 ① The Fourth Plinth가 왜 비어 있었는지 설명
  The Fourth Plinth는 원래 윌리엄 4세의 기마 동상을 세우기 위해 계획되었지만, 자금 부족으로 동상
을 완성하지 못해 150년 넘게 비어 있었다. 이 정보는 사건의 배경을 설명하는 중요한 부분이므로 반드시
포함해야 한다.

 ② The Fourth Plinth에 어떤 논의가 있었는지 시간 순서대로 서술
  1995년에 네 번째 받침대의 활용 방법에 대해 논의가 시작되었다. RSA는 대중 설문 조사를 통해
다양한 아이디어를 수집했다. 이 설문 조사에서 The Beatles, David Beckham, Winnie the Pooh와
같은 유명 인물의 동상을 세우자는 의견이 나왔다. 그러나 최종적으로 현대 미술 작품을 전시하는 공간으
로 활용하기로 결정되었다. 1998년부터 첫 번째 현대미술 작품들이 The Fourth Plinth에 전시되었고,
몇 차례의 지연이 있었다.

 ③ 최종적으로 어떤 작품이 전시되었는지와 그 의미를 서술
  2005년, Marc Quinn의 조각상 AlisonLapperPregnant가 네 번째 받침대에 전시되었다. 이 작품
은 장애를 가지고 태어난 예술가인 Alison Lapper를 표현한 것으로, 기존의 영웅 동상과는 매우 다른
의미이다. 이 조각상은 공공미술이 다양한 사람들의 이야기를 담을 수 있다는 메시지를 전달하며, 아름다
움과 영웅성의 기존 개념에 도전하는 작품이다.

  정답 해설

 지문의 밑줄 친 “studying cultures from behind a wall”은 서구 인류학자들이 지역 사람들과 직접
적으로 교류하지 않고 거리를 두며 문화를 연구했음을 의미한다. 그들은 현지 주민들과 일상생활을 공유
하거나 밀접한 상호작용을 하지 않았기 때문에 그 문화에 대한 진정한 이해를 얻기 힘들었다. 이와 같은
연구 방식은 정보가 제한적이고 편향될 가능성이 있었으며, 그들이 관찰한 사회의 복잡성과 세부적인
요소를 놓치게 되는 한계를 초래했다.
 예시 답안으로 제시한 것은 “It suggests that their research was distant and lacked true
understanding because they avoided close interaction with the local people and their daily
lives.”이다.
distant: 인류학자들이 현지 문화와 거리감을 두고 연구했음을 의미함
lacked true understanding: 직접 교류를 피했기 때문에, 관찰한 사회에 대해 진정한 이해를 얻지
 못했음을 나타냄
close interaction: 지역 주민들과 밀접한 상호작용을 피한 연구 방법을 설명
local people: 현지 사람들과의 상호작용 부족이 연구의 한계를 만든 요인으로 제시
daily lives: 인류학자들이 현지 주민들의 일상생활을 깊이 이해하지 못했음을 의미
